# Sankh

> Sankh is a lightweight API request manager. A collection is a plain folder of
> `.sh` files, each holding one `curl` command with comment annotations for
> assertions and chaining. One binary runs them in CI (`sankh run`), serves a
> local web UI (`sankh serve`), or exposes them to AI agents over MCP
> (`sankh mcp`). Requests run on the machine, never in a browser.

Docs: https://sankh.dev/docs
Source: https://github.com/sankh-dev/sankh
Full format reference: https://sankh.dev/docs/format

## Rules for agents

- Request files are shell scripts. Never run a collection the user has not
  trusted. If a run fails with "not trusted" (exit code 3), ask the user to
  review the files and run `sankh trust <path>` themselves. Do not pass
  `--trust` or set `SANKH_TRUST=1` outside CI.
- Never write secrets into `environments/*.env` (committed). Secrets go in
  `.env.local` (gitignored) or the process environment.
- Variables whose names contain TOKEN, SECRET, KEY, PASSWORD, PASSWD, AUTH or
  COOKIE are shown as `***` in all output. That is expected, not a bug.
- Prefer the machine-readable commands below over parsing human output.

## Collection layout

```
my-api/
  sankh.toml            # optional: name, default_env, timeout, [order]
  .env.example          # documents required variables, no values
  .env.local            # gitignored local values and secrets
  environments/
    dev.env             # dotenv syntax, non-secret values
  auth/01-login.sh
  users/01-list.sh
  users/02-create.sh
```

- Root: nearest folder with `sankh.toml` or `environments/`.
- Order: numeric prefix (`01-`) first by number, then alphabetical; `[order]`
  in `sankh.toml` overrides per folder.

## Request file

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# @name Create user
# @tags smoke
# @expect status 201
# @expect json .data.name == "test"
# @capture USER_ID=.data.id
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE_URL/users" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name":"test"}'
```

- Annotations live in the contiguous `#` comment block at the top (after an
  optional shebang). A blank line ends the header.
- Body: exactly one plain `curl` command is "form mode" (editable in the UI).
  Pipes, `;`, redirection or several commands are "raw mode": still runs, the
  last curl response is checked.
- Every file still runs on its own: `set -a; . environments/dev.env; set +a; sh users/02-create.sh`

## Annotations

| Annotation | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `@name <text>` | Display name |
| `@description <text>` | Notes, no effect; repeat the line for multi-line notes |
| `@tags <tag>...` | Labels for `--tag` (lowercase, digits, `-`, `_`) |
| `@timeout <duration>` | Per-request limit (`500ms`, `10s`, `2m`); overrides `timeout` in `sankh.toml` |
| `@expect status <codes>` | `200`, `2xx`, or `200\|201\|204`. Default: any 2xx |
| `@expect json <jq> <op> <value>` | Ops: `==` `!=` `>` `>=` `<` `<=` `contains` `matches "<regex>"` |
| `@expect json <jq> exists` | Non-null result |
| `@capture NAME=<source>` | Source: jq expression (`.id`), `header <Name>`, or `status` |

- Values are JSON literals: `"text"`, `42`, `true`, `null`, arrays, objects.
  Bare words are an error.
- jq expressions may contain pipes: `@expect json .items | length > 0`.
- Strings may embed variables: `@expect json .owner == "$USER_ID"`.
- Captures run only if all assertions pass, live for the current run only, and
  are available to later requests as `$NAME`.

## Environments

Lowest to highest priority: `environments/<name>.env`, `.env.local`, the
process environment, then values captured earlier in the run.

## Machine-readable commands

```bash
sankh list PATH --json                                  # request tree as JSON
sankh workspace list --json                             # saved collections + trust status
sankh run PATH --env dev --report json --report-file -  # JSON report on stdout, human output on stderr
sankh run PATH --tag smoke --folder users --bail        # filters; --bail stops at first failure
```

Exit codes for `sankh run`: 0 all passed, 1 assertion/capture/request failed,
2 usage or configuration error, 3 collection not trusted.

JSON report shape:

```json
{
  "collection": "petstore",
  "summary": { "total": 2, "passed": 1, "failed": 1, "errors": 0, "duration_ms": 41.2 },
  "results": [
    {
      "path": "pets/02-create.sh", "name": "Create pet", "outcome": "failed",
      "response": { "status": 400, "time_ms": 3.1, "headers": [["content-type", "application/json"]], "body": "..." },
      "assertions": [{ "label": "status 201", "passed": false, "message": "got 400" }],
      "captures": [], "error": null, "warnings": []
    }
  ]
}
```

## MCP server

`sankh mcp` is a stdio MCP server (read and run only, it never edits files or
grants trust). Add it to any MCP client:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "sankh": { "command": "sankh", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

With no arguments it exposes the saved workspace (see `sankh workspace add`)
plus Scratch; `sankh mcp PATH...` exposes only those folders.

Tools:

- `list_collections`: ids, names, roots, trust status.
- `list_requests(collection, tags?)`: request tree.
- `show_request(collection, path)`: file text and parsed annotations.
- `list_environments(collection)`: environment names, default, variables (secrets masked).
- `run(collection, path?, env?, folders?, tags?, bail?)`: runs requests and returns the JSON report. Refuses untrusted collections.
